title: The Snows of Kilimanjaro and the blues with three titles
summary: He appeared as saxophone soloist in the film, playing an Alfred Newman tune that had three titles.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Uh huh. Let me go back to your work in one film in the early 50's, "The Snows of Kilimanjaro". Do you recall what you did there?

Yes. Well, I appeared in the film as, you know, a saxophone soloist. I did some writing; I don't remember the extent of it now, but it was just some, you know, arranging. That was ... let's see, was that Hugo Friedhofer or was it Bernie Herman's picture.
I think that was Bernard Herman.
Bernard Herman's picture, yes. Uh huh.
A lot of people ... several people have written about that blues that you played in that film. You know, when Gregory Peck and ...what's her name ...
... Ava Gardner were in a nightclub scene or something, in Paris, was it?
Well, that was a song written by Alfred Newman, that at the time he called "Love is Cynthia" or did he change the title. It was called at one time, "Blue
Mountain" -- and then we recorded it once later in an album, and he called "To Ava" ...
